verdict.reason: Both debates separate feeling behind from wanting the milestones, test competing readings of the feeling (belonging versus expiring options or borrowed desire), narrow their claims under objection, and end with observable conditions. A is somewhat stronger on trust: it flags the limits of its own source and marks where a mind goes beyond its book. B is somewhat stronger on interaction and usefulness: the witness-bias objection widens the sample, and it splits the milestone label from the goods behind it. Neither edge would change what this user takes away.

comparisons.a_observation: The Experimenter admits that Ibarra studied career changers, not marriage, and so limits small trials to reversible choices. That produces the reversibility dividing line in A.debate[9].text.
comparisons.b_observation: The Detective objects that people who took the path are biased witnesses (sunk cost, imitation). The Forecaster answers in B.debate[4].text by widening the sample and separating the label from the goods it promises, and the Detective narrows his own claim in B.debate[9].text.
comparisons.why_it_matters: Each debate has a claim that clearly narrows under pressure and ends knowing more than it began. A's narrowing gives the user a rule for which choices to trial and which to wait on. B's gives a test of whether the milestone itself or what it stands for is the draw.

comparisons.a_observation: The phrase 'I would go further than Thoreau here' marks the belonging reading as the mind's own extension, and the critique of Ibarra's scope is calibrated.
comparisons.b_observation: The summary says the Detective treats present doubt as possibly the most honest signal, but the Detective mostly argued the feeling says little. In B.debate[7].text the Experimenter rejects withdrawing from friends, which the Detective never proposed.
comparisons.why_it_matters: These are small slips in B, but A keeps book and extension apart more cleanly. That helps a user deciding how much weight each voice deserves.

comparisons.a_observation: Its branches (drifting from friends, a real deadline, fading without comparison) end in a proportionate step: reversible experiments now, irreversible choices held until the wanting is the user's own.
comparisons.b_observation: Its branches include picturing the actual life versus the status, loss of shared time, a pull that fades when alone, and real time limits checked by talking to people on different paths, including those who chose none.
comparisons.why_it_matters: Both give conditions the user could observe. A's reversibility rule and B's label-versus-goods test are equally actionable, and both are grounded in the user's uncertainty about wanting these things.

verdict.best_of_a: A.debate[8].text: The Experimenter limits her own source's reach and draws the reversible-versus-irreversible line, which becomes the debate's most practical rule.
verdict.best_of_b: B.debate[4].text: Separating the milestone from the good it promises (a home as security, a wedding as being chosen) gives the user a concrete way to tell borrowed wanting from real wanting.

concerns.description: The summary describes the Detective as treating the user's present doubt as possibly the most honest signal, but the Detective's turns argue that the feeling says little and point to noticing private envy. The summary slightly misstates his position.
It brings in having a child, which the user never mentioned. It is framed as an example of an irreversible choice, not an assumed fact, so it does little harm.
